h: Shabbat Sanctifies the Place of Israel

p: "אִם תָּשִׁיב מִשַּׁבָּת רַגְלֶךָ וְגוֹמֵר" (יְשַׁעְיָה נח, יג),
— If you turn away your foot because of the Sabbath, etc. (Isaiah 58:13),
וְדָרְשׁוּ (עֵירוּבִין נב עַמּוּד ב) עַל אִיסּוּר תְּחוּמִין.
— and the Sages expounded (Eruvin 52b) that this verse refers to the Sabbath boundary limits (techum Shabbat).
וְיֵשׁ לְהָבִין:
— And one must understand:
דְּהָא תְּחוּמִין, אֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא, הוּא רַק בְּאִיסּוּר לָאו,
— for the restriction of techumin, even according to the opinion that it is biblically ordained, is merely a negative prohibition (punishable by lashes),
וְלָמָּה בָּחַר הַכָּתוּב דַּוְוקָא לְהַתְחִיל בִּקְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת בָּזֶה יוֹתֵר מִשְּׁאָר מְלָאכוֹת גְּמוּרוֹת,

— so why did Scripture choose to introduce the sanctification of Shabbat specifically through techumin, rather than through full, primary creative labors (melakhot gemurot) punishable by death and excision,
וַהֲוָה לֵיהּ לוֹמַר "מֵעֲשׂוֹת חֲפָצֶיךָ וְגוֹמֵר"?
— and it should rather have opened with "from doing your affairs, etc."?

p: וְכֵן עַל פָּסוּק "וַיִּחַן אֶת פְּנֵי הָעִיר" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לג, יח) דָּרְשׁוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (עט, ו) שֶׁקָּבַע תְּחוּמִין מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם,
— Likewise, on the verse "and he encamped (va-yichan) before the city" (Genesis 33:18), they expounded in Bereishit Rabbah (79:6) that Jacob instituted techumin while it was yet day,
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (שָׁם יא, ז): "יַעֲקֹב שֶׁכָּתוּב בּוֹ שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת וְכוּלֵי";
— and upon this the Sages stated (ibid. 11:7): "Jacob, concerning whom Sabbath observance is explicitly written in Scripture, etc.";
יֵשׁ לְהָבִין גַּם כֵּן: לָמָּה נִכְתַּב עַל יַעֲקֹב שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת בִּתְחוּמִין?
— and one must similarly understand: why was Jacob's exemplary Sabbath observance recorded specifically through establishing boundaries (techumin)?

p: גַּם בְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁנִּרְמַז בּוֹ שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת,
— Furthermore, regarding Abraham our father, peace be upon him, concerning whom Sabbath observance was hinted,
לְגִרְסַת הָרַשְׁבָּ"א בִּתְשׁוּבָה (חֵלֶק א סִימָן צד) וּבְסֵפֶר הָאֶשְׁכּוֹל דְּגָרְסֵי (יוֹמָא כח עַמּוּד ב):
— according to the textual reading of the Rashba (Responsa I, §94) and Sefer HaEshkol in Yoma (28b):
"קִיֵּים אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ אֲפִילּוּ עֵירוּבֵי תְּחוּמִין וְכוּלֵי",
— "Abraham our father fulfilled even eruvin for Shabbat travel boundaries, etc.,"
וְנִרְמַז בִּלְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב: "עֵקֶב אֲשֶׁר שָׁמַע אַבְרָהָם" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כו, ה),
— and this was hinted in the phrasing: "Because (eikev) Abraham hearkened" (Genesis 26:5),
שֶׁמִּלַּת "עֵקֶב" מְרַמֵּז עַל מִצְוַת תְּחוּמִין שֶׁהוּא בַּהֲלוּךְ רַגְלַיִם בְּעָקֵב;
— the word eikev (עֵקֶב) alluding to techumin, which is traversed by walking upon the heel (eikev);
גַּם בָּזֶה אֵינוֹ מוּבָן: לָמָּה רָמַז דַּוְוקָא מִצְוַת שַׁבָּת בִּתְחוּמִין?
— here too it is incomprehensible: why encode the Sabbath observance of the Patriarchs specifically through techumin?
וְאִם יִרְצֶה לְרַמֵּז לִרְבוּתָא שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ מִצְוָה קַלָּה דְּרַבָּנָן שָׁמַר – דִּסְבִירָא לֵיהּ תְּחוּמִין דְּרַבָּנָן –
— And if the intent was merely to teach a novel stringency, that he observed even a light rabbinic ordinance (holding that techumin is rabbinic),
הָיָה לוֹ לְרַמֵּז מִצְווֹת דְּרַבָּנָן קַלּוֹת מִזֶּה, וְשֶׁלֹּא בְּאִיסּוּרֵי שַׁבָּת דַּחֲמִירֵי!
— Scripture should have hinted at light rabbinic mitzvot outside of the severe domain of Sabbath laws!

footnotes.heAnchorPrefix: "קִיֵּים אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ אֲפִילּוּ עֵירוּבֵי תְּחוּמִין וְכוּלֵי",

paragraphs.text: Yoma 28b: “Apropos the previous statement, the Gemara cites that Rav said: Abraham our Patriarch fulfilled the entire Torah before it was given, as it is stated: ‘Because (ekev) Abraham hearkened to My voice and kept My charge, My mitzvot, My statutes and My Torahs’ (Genesis 26:5). Rav Shimi bar Ḥiyya said to Rav: And say that the verse means that he fulfilled only the seven Noahide mitzvot and not the entire Torah. The Gemara asks: But isn’t there also circumcision that Abraham clearly observed, which is not one of the Noahide laws? Apparently, Abraham fulfilled more than just those seven. The Gemara asks: And say that he fulfilled only the seven mitzvot and circumcision. Rav said to him: If so, why do I need the continuation of the verse, that Abraham kept: My mitzvot and My Torah? That is a clear indication that he fulfilled mitzvot beyond the seven Noahide mitzvot, and apparently fulfilled the entire Torah.”

h: The Holiness of Shabbat Enters Space

p: אַךְ הָעִנְיָן הוּא, דְּאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב, סג עַמּוּד ב):
— However, the explanation is that it is taught in the holy Zohar (Part II, 63b):
"'אַל יֵצֵא אִישׁ מִמְּקֹמוֹ בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי' (שְׁמוֹת טז, כט) –
— 'Let no man go out of his place on the seventh day' (Exodus 16:29) –
'מִמְּקֹמוֹ' תָּנֵינַן: מֵהַהוּא מָקוֹם וְכוּלֵי, וְרָזָא דְּמִלָּה: 'בָּרוּךְ כְּבוֹד ה' מִמְּקוֹמוֹ' וְכוּלֵי,
— 'from his place'—we have learned: from that specific supernal Place, and the mystery of the matter is: 'Blessed be the glory of Hashem from His place' (Ezekiel 3:12),
וְדָא אִיהוּ רָזָא דִּכְתִיב: 'כִּי הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה עוֹמֵד עָלָיו אַדְמַת קֹדֶשׁ הוּא' (שְׁמוֹת ג, ה)".
— and this is the mystery of that which is written: 'for the place whereon you stand is holy ground' (Exodus 3:5)."
כִּי זֶהוּ הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ שֶׁל קְדוּשַׁת שַׁבָּת בַּזְּמַן: לִהְיוֹת גַּם הַמָּקוֹם מְקוּדָּשׁ מִצַּד פְּרִיסַת סֻכַּת שָׁלוֹם.
— For this is the foundational root of the sanctity of Shabbat in time: that physical space (makom) likewise becomes sanctified through the spreading of the Sukkah of Peace (Sukkat Shalom).

This is the secret of the Sabbatic Crown. Therefore: ‘let no man go out of his place on the seventh day’. Blessed is the lot of him who is worthy of the glory of the Sabbath: blessed in this world and blessed in the world to come.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Bo 8:1: “‘And none of you shall go out of the door of his house until morning’ … for all of this served only to bring holiness into the dwelling-place of Israel. It follows what is written in the Zohar (II 63b): ‘Let no man go out of his place’ – from that place where it is fitting to walk, and so on; and the secret of the matter is the verse ‘Blessed be the glory of Hashem from His place,’ and this is ‘place,’ and this is the secret of ‘for the place on which you stand is holy ground.’ That is, on Shabbat the Shechinah rests in every place where a Jew dwells, for Shabbat in time is like the Sanctuary in place, the place where, even after the sin, a dwelling for the Shechinah remained among the lower beings. A person’s place is four cubits (Eruvin 48a), and, as we said, from this the Sages instituted two thousand cubits, which are five hundred times four cubits.”

It adds that Shabbat in time is like the Sanctuary in space, so that on Shabbat the Shechinah rests wherever a Jew dwells; this explains why the holiness of the day must also take hold of a place.

It adds that Shabbat in time is like the Sanctuary in space, so that on Shabbat the Shechinah rests wherever a Jew dwells; this explains why the holiness of the day must also take hold of a place.

h: Carrying Expresses the Sanctity of Place

p: וּמִפָּסוּק "אַל יֵצֵא וְגוֹמֵר" דָּרְשׁוּ עַל הוֹצָאָה מֵרְשׁוּת לִרְשׁוּת
— And from this verse "Let no man go out, etc." the Sages derived the prohibition of carrying from one domain to another
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב עֵירוּבִין יז עַמּוּד ב, וְעַיֵּין שָׁם בְּתוֹסָפוֹת);
— (as written in Eruvin 17b, and see Tosafot there);
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי מְקוֹם הַקְּדוּשָּׁה נִקְרָא "רְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד",
— meaning that the realm of holiness is termed the "Private Domain" (Reshut HaYachid), the Domain of the Singular One of the Universe,
וּ"רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים" הוּא הַהֵיפֶךְ
— whereas the "Public Domain" (Reshut HaRabbim) is the domain of fragmentation and multiplicity, the Sitra Achra
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב רֵישׁ תִּיקּוּן כד וּשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת).
— (as written at the beginning of Tikkun 24 and elsewhere).
וְעַל זֶה הִתְחִיל מַסֶּכֶת שַׁבָּת: "יְצִיאוֹת הַשַּׁבָּת" – דִּינֵי הוֹצָאָה מֵרְשׁוּת לִרְשׁוּת,
— And concerning this Tractate Shabbat opens with: "The acts of taking out on Shabbat (yetzi'ot ha-Shabbat)"—the laws of transferring between domains,
וְרָמַז: "פָּשַׁט הֶעָנִי אֶת יָדוֹ" מֵרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים שֶׁעוֹמֵד בּוֹ,
— and hints: "the poor man stretched out his hand" from the public domain where he stands,
כִּי "אֵין עָנִי אֶלָּא בְּדֵעָה" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב נְדָרִים מא עַמּוּד א);
— for "there is no poor person except one lacking da'at (spiritual awareness)" (Nedarim 41a);
וְהֲגַם שֶׁהוּא עוֹמֵד בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים, עִם כָּל זֶה יֵשׁ לוֹ גַּם שָׁם קְדוּשַׁת הַמָּקוֹם שֶׁל אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת שֶׁרַשַּׁאי לְטַלְטֵל בּוֹ בְּשַׁבָּת.
— and even though he stands physically in the public domain, he nonetheless possesses there the intrinsic sanctity of place within his four cubits, in which he is permitted to carry on Shabbat.
אָמְנָם אִם "פָּשַׁט יָדוֹ לִפְנִים וְכוּלֵי" – הֶעָנִי חַיָּיב;
— However, if "he reached his hand inside to the private domain... the poor man is liable";
וְהוּא כְּעֵין רֶמֶז רַבֵּינוּ עוֹבַדְיָה מִבַּרְטְנוּרָא עַל "פָּשַׁט בַּעַל הַבַּיִת אֶת יָדוֹ" שֶׁחַיָּיב גַּם אִם כִּיוֵּון לַעֲשׂוֹת מִצְוַת צְדָקָה,
— which parallels the Bartenura's insight that the homeowner is liable even though his intention was to perform the mitzvah of charity,
וּכְמוֹ כֵן הָרֶמֶז אֵצֶל הֶעָנִי: שֶׁגַּם אִם כִּיוֵּון בָּזֶה כְּדֵי לְעַנֵּג אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת – הוּא חַיָּיב.
— and so too regarding the poor man: even if he reached in solely to obtain food to delight the Shabbat, he is biblically liable.
וּפָתַח בּוֹ לְחִיּוּבָא דִּילֵיהּ:
— And the Mishnah opened with the case where the poor man is liable:
כִּי אֵצֶל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת הוּא מִצְוָה גְּמוּרָה מִיהַת דִּצְדָקָה לֶעָנִי,
— because for the homeowner giving food is at least an absolute mitzvah of charity,
אֲבָל גַּבֵּי הֶעָנִי הֲרֵי אָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת קיח עַמּוּד א): "עֲשֵׂה שַׁבַּתְּךָ חוֹל וְאַל תִּצְטָרֵךְ לַבְּרִיּוֹת".
— whereas for the pauper the Sages warned: "Make your Shabbat like a weekday rather than depend upon created beings."

paragraphs.text: Eruvin 17b: “Rav Ashi said: Is it written in the Torah: No man shall carry out (yotzi), indicating a prohibition against carrying objects from one domain to another on Shabbat? ‘No man shall go out (yetze)’ is written. Indeed, according to its plain meaning, the verse deals exclusively with the prohibition of going beyond the Shabbat limits and not with the prohibition of carrying out. Everyone agrees that there is no death penalty administered by the court in overstepping the Shabbat limit.”

paragraphs.text: Tosafot on Eruvin 17b: “‘A prohibition serving as the warning for a court-imposed death penalty.’ Rashi explains it as ‘one shall not carry out,’ deriving the prohibition of carrying from one domain to another. The answer is that ‘one shall not go out’ is written; there is no expression here of carrying a load.” Tosafot questions this interpretation and examines how the verse applies to carrying and to Shabbat boundaries.

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 24, 69a:3: “Bereshit: “Fear Shabbat”—you shall hold My Shabbatot in awe; fear Torah, fear the covenant. Just as the covenant must be guarded so that one does not enter it into an alien domain, so a person must guard Shabbat, not taking something out of the private domain and bringing it into the public domain. The private domain is the Shechinah: its width is four, corresponding to the four letters of the divine Name, and its height is ten, corresponding to the Name’s expanded letters. The public domain is the serpent, the woman of harlotry, the poison of the other god, Samael, who comprises the seventy nations. She is the profaned woman, and her mate is the desecration of Shabbat. Therefore one who carries from the private domain to the public domain is liable to stoning.”

paragraphs.text: Mishnah Shabbat 1:1: “The acts of taking out on Shabbat are two that are four for one inside, and two that are four for one outside. How so? The poor person stands outside and the householder inside. If the poor person extends his hand inside and places something into the householder’s hand, or takes something from it and brings it out, the poor person is liable and the householder is exempt. If the householder extends his hand outside and places something into the poor person’s hand, or takes something from it and brings it in, the householder is liable and the poor person is exempt. If the poor person extends his hand inside and the householder takes something from it, or places something into it and the poor person brings it out, both are exempt. If the householder extends his hand outside and the poor person takes something from it, or places something into it and the householder brings it in, both are exempt.”

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 118a: “The Gemara asks: Let us say that this mishna is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis and not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Ḥidka. The Gemara rejects that approach: Even if you say that it is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Ḥidka, the mishna can be understood, as we can say to him: That which you want to eat on Shabbat eve, Friday afternoon, eat at night on Shabbat instead. The Gemara asks: And do we have a person sit and fast all day on Shabbat eve? According to this suggestion, he would not eat at all on Friday. Rather, we must say: In accordance with whose opinion is this mishna? It is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Akiva, who said: Make your Shabbat like a weekday and do not be beholden to other beings. It is preferable to eat two meals on Shabbat as he does during the week if he can thereby avoid taking charity.”

p: וְשִׁינּוּי הַלָּשׁוֹן שֶׁמַּתְחִיל "יְצִיאוֹת הַשַּׁבָּת" וְלֹא "הוֹצָאוֹת",
— And regarding the linguistic anomaly of opening with yetzi'ot (יציאות) rather than hotza'ot (הוצאות),
אִיתָא בְּסִפְרֵי הַקֹּדֶשׁ שֶׁהוּא לְרַמֵּז שֵׁם יוֹ"ד–הֵ"א בְּרָאשֵׁי תֵּיבוֹת: יְ'צִיאוֹת הַ'שַּׁבָּת;
— it is taught in sacred works that the acronym spells the divine Name Yud-Hei (י-ה): Yetzi'ot HaShabbat;
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי הֵ"א הוּא בְּחִינַת הִתְגַּלּוּת מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁנִּבְרָא בְּהֵ"א (מְנָחוֹת כט עַמּוּד ב),
— for the letter Hei represents the manifestation of the Kingdom of Heaven in this world, which was created with the letter Hei,
וְיוֹ"ד מְרַמֵּז עַל עוֹלָם הַבָּא שֶׁנִּבְרָא בְּיוֹ"ד,
— and the letter Yud alludes to the World to Come, which was created with the letter Yud,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (שָׁם) עַל פָּסוּק: "כִּי בְּיָהּ ה' צוּר עוֹלָמִים" (יְשַׁעְיָה כו, ד).
— as expounded in Menachot (29b) on the verse: "for in the Lord God (Yah) is an everlasting rock".
וּבְשַׁבָּת יֵשׁ הַשְׁרָאַת הַקְּדוּשָּׁה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה גַּם כֵּן מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא.
— And on Shabbat there descends an indwelling of holiness in this world that partakes of the World to Come.

paragraphs.text: Menachot 29b: “Rava explains: They would put a hump-like stroke on the roof of the letter ḥet as if to thereby say: The Holy One, Blessed be He, lives (ḥai) in the heights of the universe. And they would suspend the left leg of the letter heh, as Rabbi Yehuda Nesia asked Rabbi Ami: What is the meaning of that which is written: ‘Trust in the Lord forever, for in the Lord (beYah) is God, an everlasting (olamim) Rock’ (Isaiah 26:4)? Rabbi Ami said to him: Anyone who puts their trust in the Holy One, Blessed be He, will have Him as his refuge in this world and in the World-to-Come. This is alluded to in the word ‘olamim,’ which can also mean: Worlds.”

h: The Boundaries of the Holy Camp

p: וּמִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַזֶּה שֶׁל הַשְׁרָאַת הַקְּדוּשָּׁה בַּמָּקוֹם
— And from this foundational root of the indwelling of holiness within space
הוּא גַּם כֵּן מִצְוַת תְּחוּמִין דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא בִּשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר מִילִין,
— derives the biblical boundary limit of twelve mil,
שֶׁהוּא הַשְׁרָאַת הַקְּדוּשָּׁה שֶׁל הַמָּקוֹם שֶׁל כָּל מַחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל.
— which is the spatial sphere of holiness encompassing the entire encampment of Israel in the wilderness (three parsa'ot by three parsa'ot = twelve mil).
וְכָל נֶפֶשׁ פְּרָטִי יֵשׁ בּוֹ כְּלָלוּת הַקְּדוּשָּׁה מִכָּל הַשִּׁיעוּר קוֹמָה שֶׁל מַחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל,
— And every individual soul contains within itself the collective holiness of the entire stature of the camp of Israel,
כְּמוֹ כָּל מִצְוָה בִּפְרָט שֶׁנִּמְצָא בָּהּ כְּלָלוּת כָּל תַּרְיַ"ג (שֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת וּשְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה) מִצְווֹת הַתְּלוּיִים בָּהּ.
— just as within each particular mitzvah is enfolded the collective matrix of all 613 commandments linked to it.
וְעַל זֶה רָמְזוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא עה עַמּוּד ב): "יְרוּשָׁלַיִם קַמַּיְיתָא תְּלָתָא פַּרְסֵי הֲוָיָא",
— And to this the Sages alluded in Bava Batra (75b): "The primordial Jerusalem measured three parsa'ot",
וְהַיְינוּ שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר מִילִין,
— which equals exactly twelve mil,
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַמָּקוֹם מְקוּדָּשׁ לְמַחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל לַאֲכִילַת קָדָשִׁים לִפְנִים מִן הַחוֹמָה.
— because that entire perimeter was sanctified as the camp of Israel for consuming holy offerings within the walls.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Shmuel Bornsztain, Shem MiShmuel, Vayishlach 11:14-18: “We have already asked why Scripture records Jacob’s Shabbat observance through techumin, which carry neither death nor karet, and not through a full melachah. My father explained that at Marah Israel were accepted only as a community and not yet each person individually. Now in all the labors of Shabbat every Jew is warned equally, but with techumin each person has his own boundary. Jacob, who was ‘whole,’ attained all the perfection that Israel attained at Sinai, the mitzvah of techumin. … The Patriarchs each comprised all of Israel, yet each also had a particular form in which he excelled, as Abraham in Chesed; Jacob, who was all-inclusive, was whole in his particular form as well. Therefore Jacob, who was accepted also in his particular form, is described through techumin, where each individual has a different boundary. Just as below each person has his boundary, so above there is a place where his soul is held, and this is ‘Let no man go out of his place on the seventh day’: his place below brings about his place above.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: Shem MiShmuel answers the os’s opening question about techumin by noting that techumin, unlike the labors of Shabbat, belong to each individual separately. Rav Tzadok makes the complementary claim that each individual soul carries the holiness of the whole camp of Israel; Shem MiShmuel adds that Jacob was perfected in his individual form, which is why his Shabbat is recorded through the individual boundary.

paragraphs.text: Bava Batra 75b: “Rabba said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: The Holy One will raise Jerusalem three parasangs upward, as it is said, ‘It shall be raised and inhabited in its place.’ What does ‘in its place’ mean? According to its original place. How do we know that its original place measured three parasangs? Rabba said: An elderly man told me: I myself saw the first Jerusalem, and it measured three parasangs.”

p: וְגַם אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה תְּחוּמִין דְּרַבָּנָן הֵם גַּם כֵּן עַל רֶמֶז קְדוּשַׁת הַמָּקוֹם:
— And even the two thousand cubits of rabbinic techumin are likewise based upon this mystery of spatial holiness:
כִּי כָּל דָּבָר תּוֹפֵס מְקוֹמוֹ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת שֶׁלּוֹ, אֲפִילּוּ בְּהַהֵיפֶךְ, כְּמוֹ צוֹאָה, וּפֶתַח זוֹנוֹת, וְהַמֵּת;
— for every entity occupies its designated domain of four cubits, even in the realm of impurity—such as excrement, the threshold of harlotry, and a corpse;
וּ"מִדָּה טוֹבָה מְרֻבָּה" עַל אַחַת חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת (תוֹסֶפְתָּא סוֹטָה פֶּרֶק ד),
— and the divine measure of goodness exceeds the measure of retribution by one to five hundred,
וְתוֹפֵס קְדוּשַׁת הַמָּקוֹם אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה, שֶׁהוּא תַּ"ק (חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת) פְּעָמִים אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת תְּפִיסַת הַהֵיפֶךְ (4 × 500 = 2,000)!
— so the holy perimeter commands two thousand cubits, which is five hundred times the four-cubit grasp of the negative side!

h: Jacob Establishes a Dwelling for Shabbat

p: וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּכְתַּב בְּיַעֲקֹב עִנְיַן חֲנִיַּת הַמָּקוֹם מִקְּדוּשַׁת מַחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל,
— And this is why regarding Jacob the camping of space is explicitly recorded as flowing from the camp of Israel,
וְהוּא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁכְּבָר נִקְבַּע בּוֹ קְדוּשַׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ;
— because the eternal sanctity of Israel was indelibly fixed within him, as we explained;
וְלָכֵן יָרַשׁ אֶת הָעוֹלָם שֶׁלֹּא בְּמִדָּה,
— wherefore he inherited the world without spatial limitation,
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁבְּכֹחוֹ לְקַדֵּשׁ גַּם מְקוֹם חוּץ לָאָרֶץ בִּקְדוּשַׁת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמוֹ בְּכָל מְקוֹם חֲנִיַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה מְקוּדָּשׁ.
— possessing the spiritual potency to sanctify even the Diaspora with the holiness of the Land of Israel, just as every encampment of Israel became consecrated.
וְלָכֵן כָּתוּב בּוֹ בְּיַעֲקֹב מְפוֹרָשׁ, שֶׁמּוֹרֶה עַל קְבִיעוּת הַקְּדוּשָּׁה לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד;
— Therefore, regarding Jacob it was written explicitly in the Torah, signifying permanent, everlasting sanctity;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ רַק בְּרֶמֶז,
— in contrast to Abraham our father, peace be upon him, regarding whom it was only hinted,
כִּי הֲגַם דְּאַבְרָהָם נִקְרָא גַּם כֵּן "יִשְׂרָאֵל",
— for even though Abraham is also titled "Israel",
"וְאֵיתָן הָאֶזְרָחִי" (תְּהִלִּים פט, א) הוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַׁת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
— being Eitan the Ezrachi (Baba Batra 15a), this status was established only through the future holiness of Jacob,
שֶׁאָז נִתְבָּרֵר קְדוּשַׁת אַבְרָהָם לְמַפְרֵעַ (וְנִתְבָּאֵר רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת וַיֵּרָא):
— when the perfection of Abraham was clarified retroactively (as explained at the beginning of Vayera):

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Maharal, Chiddushei Aggados, Shabbat 118a: “Jacob’s inheritance was without boundaries (metzarim), and for this he is called Yeshurun, for uprightness has no end, unlike what is not upright, which goes to an edge. The attribute of Jacob is Shabbat, and the Sages hinted at this when they said, ‘He encamped before the city’ – this teaches that he entered at twilight and fixed techumin for the city. We have explained that the holiness in the world is the Sabbath day, which He sanctified, and holiness is the attribute of Jacob, as has been explained many times, as it is written, ‘They shall sanctify the Holy One of Jacob.’ … What is holy and separate has no limit, for it is physical matter that has an end, since matter has extension, and whatever has extension certainly has an end. Therefore Jacob, who in particular is the holy one, has no limit to his inheritance. For insofar as Jacob was holy and more separate from matter, this has no boundary.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: Maharal also links the Midrash of Jacob’s techumin to his “inheritance without measure” through Jacob’s identity with Shabbat and holiness. He supplies the reason that holiness, being separate from matter, has no edge; Rav Tzadok expresses the same point as Jacob’s power to extend the holiness of the Land to every place Israel camps.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Sefat Emet, Vayishlach 5659 (29:5): “The Midrash states that Jacob, of whom Sabbath observance is written—“he encamped before the city,” meaning that he established boundaries—inherited the land without measure. The meaning is that on Shabbat one must establish a place of rest, for it is written, “It is a sign between Me and the children of Israel,” and “a Sabbath to the Lord in all your dwellings.” It also says “throughout their generations”: the place and dwelling of an Israelite receive the illumination of holiness on Shabbat. Thus, through establishing boundaries, the grace and illumination of Shabbat rest upon the city. The Sages said that blessing does not rest upon something measured or counted. Every measure and quantity belongs to nature, whereas blessing comes from the root, where there is no limit or measure. Therefore Shabbat, upon which blessing rests, was given only to Israel. Shabbat requires guarding, as it says, “You shall guard the Sabbath.” The boundaries separate it so that the illumination of Shabbat does not spread outside the place designated for an Israelite; there the blessing rests. For this reason the blessing subsequently extends within measure and quantity, so that it should not spread outside. As it is said, He saw that the wicked were unworthy to use the light, and separated it by concealing it within nature. Therefore Jacob, of whom Sabbath observance is written, was given the land without measure. Similarly, concerning Isaac it is taught that this estimation was for tithes: a measure made for the sake of a mitzvah is, on the contrary, a preparation for blessing to rest there.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: Sefat Emet explains why establishing a boundary can lead to an inheritance without measure: the boundary prepares and guards the place in which blessing can dwell. This develops the relation between techumin, the sanctity of place, and Jacob’s unrestricted inheritance in Rav Tzadok’s argument.
